title: Release wind-up and backoff playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Quick purpose: informal notes for a conservative 'wind-up' (final ramp) and automated backoff choreography. This is my personal scratchpad — capture heuristics, quick commands, and fuzzy thresholds we can iterate into a formal runbook.

High-level goals:
- Get stable traffic to new model/variant to target fraction with minimal user impact.
- Make rollback/backoff a single-click/quick-API operation for on-call.
- Retain ability to pin returning clients to previous variant for stateful workloads.

Definitions I use here:
- Wind-up: the last-stage aggressive ramp (e.g., 30% -> 100%) after a canary passes.
- Backoff: automatic or manual reduction of traffic to a safe variant when signals degrade.
- Safety budget: transient error budget allocated to this rollout window.

Signals to monitor (primary):
- 95/99th latency (in ms) per model route and per-region.
- Correctness/regression signals: eval-set pass-rate, hallucination score, or rerank delta (if available).
- Error rate: 5xx rate, model runtime exceptions, rate-limited responses.
- Resource saturation: GPU memory pressure, queue length, CPU steal on routing nodes.
- Cost anomalies: per-token cost jump >15% vs baseline.
- Client-side adverse signals: SDK error telemetry, client retries, user-reported failures.

Derived thresholds (starter heuristics):
- If 95th latency > baseline + 2x stddev OR absolute > 2s for two consecutive 1-minute windows => auto-step down.
- If 5xx rate > 0.5% of requests for 5 minutes => immediate hold and alert.
- If correctness regression on eval-set > 5% in rolling 1h => hold and notify ML team.
- If GPU memory pressure > 85% for 10m => step down and increase warmup cohorts.

Wind-up sequence (manual + automated blend):
1) Pre-wind safety checks (30m before): verify canary telemetry green, review recent deploys, pre-warm caches (run priming queries: small set of representative prompts).
2) Open a release channel (Slack) and pin stakeholder list (SRE, ML, ProdEng, Customer Success).
3) Configure gradual ramp schedule: +10% every 5–10 minutes for low-risk routes; +20% every 15 minutes for high-confidence, internal-only routes. Document the exact schedule in the release thread.
4) On each increment: run the small smoke test suite (latency, top-k correctness on golden prompts, and a quick load test at the increment size). Use automated job: ci/release-smoke.sh --fraction CURRENT.
5) After reaching 60%: lengthen observation windows to 15m and check long-tail latency and cost. Increase safety budget holdback to allow manual pauses.
6) Final push to 100% only if 3 consecutive observation windows pass and there are no open alerts.

Backoff choreography (automated options):
- Soft step-downs: reduce traffic by the last increment size immediately when early-warning signals fire. Helps isolate dose-response.
- Quick abort: route all traffic to the prior pinned variant (fast path) when hard thresholds hit (5xx spike, memory OOM, or correctness regression).
- Spillover: route traffic from a failing region to nearest healthy region for a short period if latency budget allows.

Pinning rules (client affinity):
- Use a deterministic header-based pin: X-RW-Variant: <variant-id>. SDKs can cache this and include on future requests. Store the pin TTL (default 24h) and an opt-out header to unpin.
- For model-flip cases where embeddings/state matter, create a migration window: pinned clients get a grace period where both variants are supported or translation layer enabled.
- Admin API: PATCH /releases/pin?client=<id>&variant=<id>&ttl=SECONDS — keep audit log for each pin request.

Operational commands (quick):
- Manual step-down to previous variant: POST /traffic/route { "to": "variant-old", "fraction": 100 }
- Reduce incremental ramp: POST /traffic/schedule { "fraction_delta": -10 }
- Snapshot current routing: GET /traffic/snapshot -> store in release thread (useful for later analysis).

Observability checklist for the channel during wind-up:
- Live dashboards: per-route latency heatmap, cost per token, GPU utilization, error rate by code.
- Attach the smoke job output to the thread automatically.
- Have quick queries ready in Observatory: request sample ids for failed requests, top prompt prefixes for slow tails.

Fall-through and postmortem seeds:
- If we back off: save the exact snapshot of traffic distribution + model versions + kernel/quantization flags. Must be reproducible.
- Collect a 1k-sample of requests from the tail 5% before and after backoff to compare outputs.
- Note stateful client churn: did pins cause a spike in version-mismatch errors?

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Who owns the automatic backoff thresholds? Ops or Platform? We need a governance doc.
- Decide default pin TTL and whether SDKs should auto-refresh pins. Action: propose default 24h, discuss with SDK owners.
- Should we have a canned 'decay to 0%' rollout mode for extremely urgent failures (graceful wind-down over 2 minutes)?
- Add a lightweight canary that runs golden prompts through model variants at 1% of traffic continuously (bring-your-own tests).

Notes to self (short-term action items):
- Add small script to run priming queries against new variant: tools/prime_variant.py --variant X --region us-west1.
- Wire alerting to runbook links in Slack; pre-populate the release channel with the commands above.
- Draft a mini-runbook for on-call that lists the three quick buttons: step-down, abort-to-previous, pin-client.

Post-release stabilization ideas:
- Hold 10% of safety budget for 24h to allow quick roll-forward if small regressions are fixed.
- If cost increases marginally but latency improves, consider 'cost-mode' route to steer non-SLA traffic to cheaper quantized variant.

Rough incident story templates (for postmortem):
- Timeline: deploy start, each ramp increment timestamp, first alert, initial action, final resolution.
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel selection, warm cache miss, model regression, or infra saturation.
- Action items: short-term mitigation + long-term fix + owner + ETA.

Small snippets I keep reusing:
- "When in doubt, hold. When sure, automate."
- "Decant slowly; panics are expensive."

End of scratchpad. Will polish into a canonical release runbook after 2–3 real wind-ups and a retro.
